chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from 'Ali ibn Ya'qub, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I only instructed Aba al-Khattab to perform the maghrib salat when the redness disappears from the east of the sun’s rise; but he took it to mean the redness that is on the side of the west, so he used to perform salat when the twilight disappeared.

key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: the redness in the sky, used here as a sign for prayer timing
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the maghrib salat, the sunset prayer
key_terms.مَطْلِعِ الشَّمْسِ: the place of the sun’s rising, meaning the eastern direction
key_terms.مِنْ قِبَلِ الْمَغْرِبِ: from the direction of the west

ai.seo_question: When does the time of maghrib salat begin according to this hadith from al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the time of maghrib salat by distinguishing between the redness in the east and the twilight in the west. It indicates that a mistaken understanding of the Imam’s instruction led to delaying the prayer until the western twilight vanished.
